newsitem.title: USA: Pulitzer Prize winner for editorials looks locally.
newsitem.headline: Pulitzer Prize winner for editorials looks locally.

text.p: The newly named winner of the Pulitzer Prize for editorial writing said Monday he was perfectly content writing for and about the 50,000 residents of Ames.

The reason for his contentment may be that Michael Gartner, 58, had already reached the pinnacle of journalism as the former president of NBC News. Even in that post, he "commuted" from his home state of Iowa.
"I own this newspaper with two friends and am having a great time doing it," Gartner told Reuters from the Daily Tribune's newsroom.
"I try to be a good reporter, and give my opinion and then give it to the community," Gartner said.

Among the issues Gartner has written about have been the propriety of "lap dancing" offered in local strip bars, the placement of billboards, and controversies over economic development in the university town. He also occasionally writes about the origins of select words.
The newspaper's staff of 18 was celebrating with him, Gartner said. He added, "You're always happy" when such an honour is bestowed.
"I'll be doing this the rest of my life. I'm an Iowan," said Gartner, who was born and raised 30 miles away in Des Moines. "This is a great town. A terrific town."
